after: ## Family structures and their strengths and limitations
alt: Simple family trees for eight structures: nuclear, horizontal extended, vertical or beanpole extended, modified extended (kin living apart but in contact), reconstituted with step-children, lone parent, empty nest and childless.
caption: Each structure is a different arrangement of adults, children and generations.

alt: Five dimensions of diversity from Rapoport and Rapoport (1982): organisational, cultural (such as extended households and kibbutzim), class (such as Bethnal Green), life course and cohort. A note says ethnic patterns should be explained by culture, migration history and economic position.
caption: Diversity has more than one dimension.

alt: Three views of diversity. The New Right see it as decline, linking lone parenthood to an underclass, though critics point to poverty. Chester argues it is exaggerated: most people live in a nuclear family at some stage. Postmodernists see it as freedom of choice, though choice is constrained.
caption: Decline, freedom, or exaggeration: three readings of the same trend.

alt: A person who lived in a nuclear family earlier in life is in a single-person household today. A household count captures only today, which is why Chester argues snapshot statistics overstate diversity.
caption: A single snapshot can hide a life spent mostly in nuclear families.

alt: Every family is a household, but not every household is a family. Alongside families related by blood, marriage, civil partnership or adoption sit three alternatives: single person households, shared households of unrelated adults, and friends as family.
caption: Use “family” and “household” precisely: the alternatives are households, not families.

alt: Types of marriage grouped by question: how many spouses (monogamy, serial monogamy), how the partner is chosen (arranged, which is not forced, or love), and what the relationship is like (empty shell, not to be confused with empty nest).
caption: Group marriage types by number, choice and quality of relationship.
